body.statement: The identified set of profile-specific CATE curves is exactly \(\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}=\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). The set \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is nonempty, compact, and convex in \(\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}\).
body.justification: The theorem replaces unrelated pointwise intervals by the joint law-sharp function-valued causal object.
body.gap: Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari characterize random-set expectations abstractly, while Wang et al. give only covariatewise survival-CATE endpoints; neither identifies this dropout obstacle image.
body.consumer: The sharp compact set is the target needed for honest sign statements along a prognostic score and across genomic profiles.
body.proof_tex:
Define the causal identified set, without reference to the proposed observed-law functional, by
\[
\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
:=\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}
\subset\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}.                                        \qquad\text{(1)}
\]
We first prove \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Fix \(P\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  On \(\{A=a\}\), consistency and the definition \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{C\leq T\}\) imply
\[
T(a)=\widetilde T+(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta.                            \qquad\text{(2)}
\]
Indeed, if \(\Delta=0\), then \(C>T(a)\) and \(\widetilde T=T(a)\); if \(\Delta=1\), (2) is tautological.  Conditional randomization, together with treatment overlap so that the arm conditional expectation is defined, now yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[T(a)\mid Z=z,R=r]
&=E_P[T(a)\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\\
&=b_{a,z}(r)+s^P_{a,z}(r).                                               \qquad\text{(3)}
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the second equality follows from (2), compatibility with \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and the residual-contribution definition.  Subtracting (3) for \(a=0\) from (3) for \(a=1\) gives
\[
\tau_z^P(r)=b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+s^P_{1,z}(r)-s^P_{0,z}(r).            \qquad\text{(4)}
\]

Bounded event time also gives, on \(\{A=a\}\),
\[
0\leq (T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta
\leq(t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta.                                    \qquad\text{(5)}
\]
Conditional expectation and the dropout-capacity definition therefore imply
\[
0\leq s^P_{a,z}(r)\leq u_{a,z}(r)                                      \qquad\text{(6)}
\]
for the conditional score law almost every \(r\).  The model-class restrictions make \(s^P_{a,z}\) \(L\)-Lipschitz and make \(u_{a,z}\) H\"older continuous.  Profile positivity makes the following conditional densities well defined, and Bayes' rule, treatment overlap, and the score-density bound give
\[
\frac{dP_{\mathrm{obs}}(R\in dr\mid A=a,Z=z)}{dr}
=\frac{\pi_a(z,r)p_z(r)}{P_{\mathrm{obs}}(A=a\mid Z=z)}
\geq\varepsilon c_p>0.                                                  \tag{7}
\]
A strict violation of either inequality in (6) at one point would, by continuity, persist on an interval having positive conditional probability by (7), contradicting (6) almost surely.  Thus (6) holds for every \(r\in[0,1]\).  Residual monotonicity and residual Lipschitz continuity then give
\[
s^P_{a,z}\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\qquad\text{for every }a,z. \qquad\text{(8)}
\]
Equations (4) and (8) prove the desired outer inclusion.

For the reverse inclusion, take any
\[
g=(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f_{1,z}-f_{0,z})_{z\in\mathcal Z}
\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\]
The completion-witness lemma supplies a single full-data law \(P^f\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) satisfying \(s^{P^f}_{a,z}=f_{a,z}\) simultaneously for every arm, profile, and score.  Equation (4), applied to \(P^f\), gives \(\tau^{P^f}=g\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\]
which, together with the outer inclusion, proves law sharpness rather than only validity.

We finally establish the geometric assertions.  For fixed \((a,z)\), the zero function belongs to \(\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), so the set is nonempty.  Its defining pointwise interval, monotonicity, and Lipschitz inequalities are preserved by convex combinations, so it is convex.  They are also preserved under uniform limits, so it is closed in \(C([0,1])\).  Moreover,
\[
\|f\|_\infty\leq\|u_{a,z}\|_\infty,
\qquad |f(r)-f(r')|\leq L|r-r'|.                                      \qquad\text{(9)}
\]
The first bound is finite because \(u_{a,z}\) is continuous on \([0,1]\).

For completeness, compactness follows directly from (9).  Given any sequence \((f_k)\) in the obstacle set, enumerate a countable dense subset of \([0,1]\).  At each dense point the scalar sequence is bounded.  Its convergent-subsequence extraction follows constructively by enclosing its values in a bounded interval, repeatedly retaining a half-interval containing infinitely many terms, and choosing increasing indices from the resulting nested intervals; their diameters tend to zero.  Repeating this extraction over the countable dense set and taking the diagonal subsequence produces a subsequence converging at every point of that dense set.  Given \(\epsilon>0\), choose a finite dense-subset net with mesh less than \(\epsilon/(3L)\).  Convergence on the finitely many net points and (9) imply, for all sufficiently large \(k,\ell\),
\[
\sup_{r\in[0,1]}|f_k(r)-f_\ell(r)|
\leq 2L\frac{\epsilon}{3L}+\frac{\epsilon}{3}=\epsilon.               \qquad\text{(10)}
\]
Thus the extracted subsequence is uniformly Cauchy, has a continuous uniform limit, and closedness puts that limit back in the obstacle set.  Every sequence therefore has a convergent subsequence; because the ambient norm topology is metric, \(\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is compact.

There are only \(2|\mathcal Z|\) obstacle factors, so their product is nonempty, compact, and convex.  The affine map
\[
(f_{a,z})_{a,z}\longmapsto
(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f_{1,z}-f_{0,z})_{z\in\mathcal Z}                    \qquad\text{(11)}
\]
is continuous, since the sup-norm distance between two images is at most twice the largest sup-norm distance between their coordinates.  Its image is exactly \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Continuous images preserve compactness, and affine images preserve convexity.  The image is nonempty because the product is nonempty.  This proves all claims.
